dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Para localizar um valor maior que 1 na reta, ajuda saber quantas unidades inteiras ele contém. Como você pode separar 33/12 em inteiros e uma fração menor que 1?

Clique no botão 'Convert'. Isso abrirá campos para a parte inteira e a fração. O enunciado já deu uma pista: ele menciona '2 e 9/12'. Tente colocar o 2 no campo da parte inteira e o 9/12 nos campos da fração.
O campo 'm1' é para o número inteiro (2). Os campos 'm2' e 'm3' são para a fração (9 e 12). Preencha-os e veja se o sistema aceita.
Após clicar em 'Convert', digite '2' no campo 'm1', '9' no campo 'm2' e '12' no campo 'm3'. Isso representa exatamente o número misto que você precisa para marcar na reta.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 12 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: Look at the top number in the fraction. It tells how many pens are being counted.
Read the fraction from top to bottom and identify the number before the fraction bar.
The total number of pens is the top number of .../12.
Type the total number of pens into field f1.
Think about the size of one group used to measure the pens.
Read the bottom number of the fraction and connect it to the number of pens in one dozen.
One dozen contains twelve pens.
Type the number of pens in one dozen into field f2.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to decide whether the fraction is greater than one.
When the numerator is larger than the denominator, use the conversion control to rewrite the improper fraction.
Here, 33 is larger than 12, so the fraction represents more than one dozen.
Select the button that opens the mixed-number fields.
A mixed number has a whole-number part and a fractional part.
Divide 33 by 12. Use the quotient as the whole-number part and the remainder as the fractional numerator.
Twelve goes into 33 twice, and subtracting 24 from 33 leaves 9.
Enter the quotient in m1, the remainder in m2, and keep the original denominator in m3.
Use the whole-number part first, then place the remaining fraction after that whole number.
Start at 2 and divide the interval from 2 to 3 into 12 equal parts.
Move 9 of the 12 equal intervals to the right of 2.
Place the point three quarters of the way from 2 to 3.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and its location represent the same quantity.
Verify the numerator, denominator, mixed-number fields, and position on the number line.
The fraction should read 33/12, and the point should be between 2 and 3.
When the fields and point are correct, select the button that submits the task.

Katie has a huge collection of colorful pens; she has 33 of them! If she were to describe the pen collection in number of dozens, it would be 33/12, or 2 and 9/12 dozens. Show the number of dozens of pens on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?
